- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.11 or 0.00); model tends to overshoot into next period.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.22 or -0.28) — model fails to account for downward pressure.
- Lagging mean reversion: model often holds prices too high for 2–3 periods after a spike, then corrects — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per lagged period.
- When sentiment is mixed or trending neutral, model overreacts to short-term volatility — dampen forecast volatility by 10–15%.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) — reduce initial forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with true mean.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward — apply a downward correction of 0.3–0.8% per negative sentiment unit.
